saints.name: St. Fulbert of Chartres
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop and teacher who made Chartres a beacon of learning and rebuilt its great cathedral…
biography: Born about 960, of humble stock and probably in Picardy, Fulbert studied at the cathedral school of Reims, where a fellow student was the future king Robert the Pious, and by tradition under Gerbert of Aurillac, later Pope Sylvester II. Called to Chartres, he directed its cathedral school and drew scholars from many lands; his pupils named him the 'venerable Socrates'.

Made deacon in 1004 and bishop of Chartres in 1006, he governed for twenty-two years, counselling kings and prelates in letters still read; that to Duke William V of Aquitaine, on the mutual duties of lord and vassal, became a classic of feudal law. When his cathedral burned in 1020 he raised the funds to rebuild it; his crypt survives beneath the present church.

A fervent servant of the Virgin, whose relic the Sancta Camisia Chartres treasured, he spread the feast of her Nativity through his sermon Approbate consuetudinis and left the Easter hymn Chorus novae Jerusalem ('Ye choirs of new Jerusalem'). He died on 10 April 1028; never formally canonized, he is honored as a saint at Chartres and stands in the Roman Martyrology.
saints.knownFor: The school of Chartres and the rebuilding of its cathedral.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 10 April
